did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm’s title identifies it as “A Shiggaion of David” and connects the song with the words of Cush the Benjaminite against David.
Did you know? David begins by declaring that the LORD is his refuge and asking Him to save him from all his pursuers.
Did you know? To convey the intensity of the danger, David uses the image of a lion tearing his soul apart, with no one to rescue him.
Did you know? David presents his claim conditionally: if he has done wrong or there is guilt on his hands, he must answer for it.
Did you know? David considers the possibility that he repaid evil to someone who was at peace with him or released his enemy without cause; in this way, he puts his innocence to a clear moral test.
Did you know? David asks the LORD to rise and awaken judgment against his enemies, using language that portrays the LORD as a judge acting in a public arena.
Did you know? Alongside his request for judgment on the nations, David asks the LORD to judge him according to his righteousness and integrity.
Did you know? The psalm emphasizes that the LORD examines not only outward actions but also the heart and the innermost thoughts, which are presented as the objects of His examination.
Did you know? One of the psalm’s central images is that the wicked fall into the pit they themselves have dug; their evil deeds thus turn against them.
Did you know? The psalm ends with thanksgiving and song: David gives thanks to the LORD for His righteousness and praises the name of the Most High.
